newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Kuzbassenergo power utility plans '97 ADR.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Kuzbassenergo power utility plans '97 ADR.

text.p: Russian regional power utility Kuzbassenergo plans to issue level-one American Depositary Receipts to allow its shares to trade on foreign markets in the second half of this year, the company said on Wednesday.
Spokesman Valery Plyushchev said the board of directors at the Siberian power utility had approved the programme, which will now get under way, on Tuesday.

He was unable to say whether shareholders who meet in early June will have to approve the plan but said Cleary, Gottlieb, Steen & Hamilton would be the company's financial consultant and the Bank of New York its depositary.
"There is the possibility that Price Waterhouse will make an international standard audit this year," Plyushchev said.
He declined to give preliminary results for 1996 which will be approved at the annual meeting.
Rye, Man & Gor Securities said Kuzbassenergo's pretax profit for the first 11 months of 1996 was $63 million after $191 million in 1995 and 1995 net profit was $141 million.
An analyst said he did not expect a dividend for 1996 and that profits were down as receivables had almost doubled in 1996 on 1995 and revenues were directed towards reinvestment.
The brokerage said company shares, which are not listed on the Russian Trading System (RTS) or the RTS-2 system of less liquid shares, were trading at $0.37, up from about $0.11 in December 1996.
Plyushchev said national power company RAO UES owned 49 percent of Kuzbassenergo, workers and management had 18 percent and investors owned the remainder.
The company has 606 million ordinary shares with a nominal value of 1,000 roubles each, he said.
